# Landscape: factories x components

How other products handle the components covered in lesson 1: whether a person approves or edits the plan first,
whether the plan becomes tasks that outlive the chat, whether those tasks carry criteria and dependencies,
what judges a task done, whether the loop moves on to the next task by itself, and who drives that loop. Lesson 2 adds
the design step: whether the planner reads the code first, what form its design takes, whether it names reuse or risks,
who approves before work starts, and how the plan becomes tasks. Twelve depth dimensions follow: whether it asks questions
first, lists assumptions, lets the person edit the plan, where the plan is saved, ordering, parallel split, re-planning,
second-model critique, how read-only is enforced, tracker output, a human-only flag and a rollout section. Lesson 3 adds eight verification depth dimensions: whether it runs tests or
linters itself, turns acceptance criteria into checks, plans tests per task, is gated by CI or branch protection, sets
coverage or run limits, guards against weakened tests, shows logs or visual evidence, and fixes after the PR opens. Lesson 4 adds eight PR routing dimensions: whether it reviews new PRs on its own,
re-reviews after a push, can approve, fixes review comments, red CI and merge conflicts itself, limits its rounds, and where
the PR state lives. Lesson 5 adds nine activity visibility dimensions: whether it shows a list of current work, a status
per item, why an item is waiting, a run log, the history of finished work, the link to the PR, why the agent did something,
cost per item, and whether it works as one local agent with no hosted account. Each cell is
a paraphrase of a first-party page, with its source URL and the date it was fetched. Cells we could not source are
omitted, not guessed. Task-queue options are not compared per component; they get one Queue column.

**Names are not canonical.** The bold text in each cell is the product's own name for the
capability, taken from its docs. The same stage goes by different names in different factories.

### Task-queue options

| Product | Queue | Demoable | Where it takes it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Linear | Issues, Projects, Cycles **Issues, Projects, Cycles**: Issues are Linear's fundamental unit of work; Projects group issues around a shared outcome, and Cycles are a team's repeating planning period. ([source](https://linear.app/docs/conceptual-model), as of 2026-10-10) | unknown | unknown |
| Jira | Work items **Work items (formerly issues)**: Work items are the building blocks of Jira and can represent a story, bug, task or another work type. ([source](https://support.atlassian.com/jira-software-cloud/docs/what-is-an-issue/), as of 2026-10-10) | unknown | unknown |
| GitHub Issues | Issues, sub-issues, Projects **Issues, sub-issues, Projects**: Issues track bugs, features and ideas; sub-issues add hierarchies between issues, and Projects is integrated with issues to plan and track a team's work. ([source](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/learning-about-issues/about-issues), as of 2026-10-10) | unknown | unknown |

- OpenHands / CI or branch protection gates: Pages checked: Goal Completion Loop (docs.openhands.dev). CI or branch gating is not documented for the goal loop.
- OpenHands / Guard against weakened tests: Pages checked: Goal Completion Loop (docs.openhands.dev). Not documented as a rule; the judge reads real output, which covers false claims, not edited tests.
- OpenHands / Fixes after the PR opens: Pages checked: Goal Completion Loop (docs.openhands.dev). Post-PR fixes are not documented for the goal loop.

- OpenHands / Test-quality measure (mutation score or similar): Page checked: Goal Completion Loop (docs.openhands.dev). Nothing grades the tests. Not documented; checked on 2026-10-29.

None says plan steps carry acceptance criteria. Multi-agent help says Build in Parallel keeps dependent steps in order but not how dependencies are written.

The pages say a plan is made before writing any code but do not say whether edit tools are withheld or the agent is only told not to edit, so no label is given. Not documented.

- Cursor / Rollout or rollback section: Pages checked: Plan Mode, Plan mode help, Cursor Agent, Multi-agent help (cursor.com, Plan Mode). The separate Rollouts feature writes a rollout plan when a pull request opens, which is a different artifact from this plan. Not documented.

- Cursor / Per-task test plan: Pages checked: cloud-agent, capabilities, best-practices (cursor.com/docs). Per-task test planning is not documented.

Other pages do: the `/verify` and `/run` skills, Chrome and Computer use (see landscape/verify-grid/claude-code.md).

- Claude Code / Parallel split of independent work: Pages checked: Permission modes, Best practices, Common workflows, Large codebases (code.claude.com). Parallel work is a separate choice: worktrees, subagents, agent teams or /batch. Not documented.

- Claude Code / Rollout or rollback section: Pages checked: Permission modes, Best practices, Common workflows, Tools reference (code.claude.com, Plan mode), Large codebases. The only rollback and rollout hits are unrelated. Not documented.

No CI or branch gating is set up by default. code-review-pull-requests does document a conversation-resolution branch-protection note and a scripted severity-count gate (see landscape/verify-grid/claude-code.md).

## Updating

1. Edit `landscape/matrix.json`. Every populated cell needs `name` (the product's own term,
   or the literal `unknown` if its docs give none), `summary` (a paraphrase of the page),
   `sourceUrl` (https, on a host listed in the product's `allowedHosts`), `asOf`
   (`YYYY-MM-DD`, the day you fetched the page), and `short` (at most 8 words, the text a
   slide cell shows; name the surface when a product has two), and `chip` (the compact text a
   slide cell shows, in the format below). Factories carry one cell per component; task-queue
   products carry one `queue` cell. Omitted cells have no chip; slides show `–` for them.
2. `chip` format by component:
   - Marks (`plan-hitl`, `plan-persist`, `plan-contents`, `verify-runs-app`, `loop-includes-plan`,
     `design-reads`, `design-reuse`, and the depth marks `plan-clarify`, `plan-assumptions`, `plan-editable`,
     `plan-ordering`, `plan-parallel`, `plan-replan`, `plan-critique`, `plan-tracker`, `plan-human-only`, `plan-rollout`, and the
     verify marks `verify-checks`, `verify-criteria`, `verify-test-plan`, `verify-ci-gate`, `verify-limits`,
     `verify-test-guard`, `verify-pr-fix`, `verify-hidden-tests`, `verify-test-quality`, and the routing marks `route-trigger`, `route-rereview`,
     `route-approve`, `route-fix-comments`, `route-fix-ci`, `route-fix-conflicts`, `route-limits`, and the activity marks
     `act-list`, `act-status`, `act-reason`, `act-log`, `act-history`, `act-pr-link`, `act-why`, `act-cost`, `act-local`):
     exactly one of `✓` (yes), `✗` (no, only where a cited page states it), `◐` (partly or mixed).
   - Labels, one or two joined by ` + `: `verify-judge` from Check, Model, Agent, Person;
     `verify-keeps-going` from Goal, Hook, Auto-fix, Prompt, Autopilot; `loop-starts-next` from
     Event, Schedule, Finished run, Person; `design-form` from File, Chat; `design-approval`
     from Human, Human approves, Automated; `design-tasks` from Plan steps, Parallel, Tickets, Same session;
     `plan-saved` from File, Chat; `plan-readonly` from Tool restriction, Instruction only; `verify-evidence`
     from Logs, Visual; `route-state` from GitHub, Own app.
   - Names (`plan-name`, `execute-name`, and a task-queue `queue` cell): the product's own term,
     at most 3 words, never a docs page title.
3. `demoable` and `destination` need the same source and date unless they are explicitly
   `unknown` (`kind: "unknown"` / `summary: "unknown"`).
4. If you cannot find a first-party page that supports a cell, replace it with
   `{ "omitted": "reason" }`; the reason names the pages checked. Never fill a cell from memory.
5. Run `bun scripts/render-landscape.ts` to regenerate this file, then
   `bun scripts/check-landscape.ts` (also run in CI) to validate.
